provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: AT WORDS 0-0: typica 'Deus,' vs the 1862 Pustet 'BEus,'; AT WORDS 3-3: typica 'hodierna' vs the 1862 Pustet 'hodi6rna'; AT WORDS 5-12: typica 'Exalttionis sanctae Crucis annua solemnitate laetificas: praesta, qusesumus;' vs the 1862 Pustet 'Exaltati6nis sancteeCrucis ma solemnitte lsetiticas: prsesta. qwesumus;'; the 1862 Pustet prints 'ut' where the typica prints 'ut,' (pointing only); the 1862 Pustet spells 'cujus' where the typica spells 'cuius' (orthography/accent only); AT WORDS 15-15: typica 'mystrium' vs the 1862 Pustet 'mystenum'; AT WORDS 18-18: typica 'cognovimus,' vs the 1862 Pustet 'cogn6vimus,'; the 1862 Pustet spells 'ejus' where the typica spells 'eius' (orthography/accent only); AT WORDS 20-20: typica 'redemptionis' vs the 1862 Pustet 'redempti6nis'; the 1862 Pustet spells 'coelo' where the typica spells 'caelo' (orthography/accent only); AT WORDS 24-24: typica 'mereamur.' vs the 1862 Pustet 'meremur.'; AT WORDS 26-27: typica 'eundem Dominum.' vs the 1862 Pustet 'eftmdein D6minum.'; AT WORDS 0-0: typica 'Deus,' vs the 1922 Mame 'EUS,'; AT WORDS 5-6: typica 'Exalttionis sanctae' vs the 1922 Mame 'Exaltationis sanctz'; the 1922 Mame spells 'letificas' where the typica spells 'laetificas:' (orthography/accent only); the 1922 Mame spells 'presta,' where the typica spells 'praesta,' (orthography/accent only); AT WORDS 12-12: typica 'qusesumus;' vs the 1922 Mame 'quesumus;'; the 1922 Mame spells 'cujus' where the typica spells 'cuius' (orthography/accent only); AT WORDS 15-15: typica 'mystrium' vs the 1922 Mame 'mysterium'; the 1922 Mame spells 'ejus' where the typica spells 'eius' (orthography/accent only); the 1922 Mame spells 'premia' where the typica spells 'praemia' (orthography/accent only); the 1922 Mame spells 'celo' where the typica spells 'caelo' (orthography/accent only); AT WORDS 26-26: typica 'eundem' vs the 1922 Mame 'eumdem'. Corroboration: Two independent public-domain witnesses were read for every oration: the Pustet Ratisbon 1862 whole-book text layer and the Tours: Mame 1922 editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (artifact ia-scan-pdf-9873693a), the latter reconstructed column by column from its page word bounding boxes. The Vatican typica 1604 and Venice 1570 were swept but not relied on (both are registered degraded-latin and their records forbid resting a claim on a raw search over them).. Recorded limitation: || REPAIRED by lane repair-2 on 2026-09-03. The stored target had been a text-layer reading carrying recogniser damage; it has been replaced word for word by a reading taken from the 1962 CMAA facsimile page image at 400 dpi (artifact PDF p. 735, printed folio read on the same image). Line-end hyphens are joined, printed stress accents are dropped, and the ae/oe ligatures are expanded to two letters; punctuation, capitalisation and the conclusion are reproduced at the length the page prints them. The verdict, the antecedent locus and the recorded differences are the original lane's and were not revisited. The marginal number 3606 already in the locus was confirmed on the same 400 dpi image; it is set on the first line of the oration, immediately after the half of the hyphenated word that ends that line, which is why the CMAA text layer swallowed it into the body text.
